clue.text: Mouth-opening lets down many an actor

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the thing that does the lowering, a stage device in the floor

parts.note: trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'
a door is an opening into a room

explanation.surface: An actor is let down by what comes out of his open mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lets down' reads as disappoints, but it means literally lowers: a stage trap drops actors below the boards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage trap in the floor lowers performers out of sight during a play.

clue.text: Hybrid fruit said to have nothing of the peach in it

indicators.note: said tells us the word meant is only heard, and a different spelling is entered

parts.words: to have nothing of the peach in it
parts.note: a peach is slang for a beauty, so having none of it is being plain-looking

explanation.surface: A cross-bred fruit is reputed to share nothing with the peach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peach' looks like the fruit, but it is the slang for a beautiful person; a face with nothing of the peach is ugly, which sounds like the fruit's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican cross between a grapefruit and a tangerine.

clue.text: Noble Century, it turns out, taken all together

indicators.note: these words suggest something being rearranged, so the letters of noble and C are reshuffled

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A noble scores a hundred, and everything taken together, it turns out well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' rearranges NOBLE plus C into the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means as a whole, all at once, said of things handled as one lot.

clue.text: Potential wooer fastening on belt

definitions.meaning: in the fairy tale a ... kissed by a princess turns into a prince who woos her
a loop or attachment on a belt for carrying a sword or bayonet

explanation.surface: A would-be suitor does up the buckle of his belt.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale amphibian becomes a prince and suitor; separately, the word names a sword-holding loop on a belt.

clue.text: Traction so variable in drawer for papers

indicators.note: variable means changeable, so the letters of traction and so are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Traction is so changeable inside a newspaper office drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture for storing papers, but it means a person who draws, for the newspapers; 'variable' shuffles TRACTION and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper cartoon is the work of an artist who draws comic pictures for the press.

clue.text: Flight taking one into the Milky Way, for example

indicators.note: taking means the word for the galaxy's lights takes in, or holds, the other piece

parts.note: the Milky Way is a band of stars across the night sky
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A flight that takes someone up into the Milky Way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel to the stars, but it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps leading from one floor to another.

clue.text: Interpreter has to go slowly approaching sultanate

indicators.note: approaching means the first piece comes up to and just before the next one

parts.note: to drag is to move slowly and tediously
Oman is an Arabian sultanate

explanation.surface: A translator has to go slowly on the way into an Arab sultanate.
explanation.walkthrough: A dragoman is an interpreter or guide in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking countries, fitting the Middle Eastern surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an official translator and guide in the Middle East.

clue.text: Instrument to help bartender, say, with correct measure?

definitions.text: Instrument to help bartender, say, with correct measure?

parts.words: Instrument to help bartender, say, with correct measure?
parts.note: read as a bar-tender, a musician tending the bars of a piece, who needs a ticking device to keep the beat in each measure

explanation.surface: A gadget that helps a barman pour the right measure of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bartender' and 'measure' point to a pub; in music a measure is a bar, and the device keeps the player's tempo correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A clockwork ticker sets a steady beat for musicians practising, keeping each bar in time.

clue.text: Nothing on trial, sadly, in the market-place

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the following piece comes after
sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of trial are jumbled

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A trial goes badly for someone with nothing, held in the town market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue puts the zero after the shuffled word. The Rialto was the exchange district of Venice, the market-place mentioned in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice's Rialto was the city's trading quarter, its commercial exchange.

clue.text: Inapt, changing colour

indicators.note: changing means the letters of inapt are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Something unsuitable altering its hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint is a coloured coating applied to surfaces, and a colour is its result.

clue.text: Merry tune — number one in Windscale, say?

definitions.meaning: Windscale stands for the Beaufort wind scale, whose force one is a gentle breeze; Windscale was also a Cumbrian nuclear site

explanation.surface: A jolly song is top of the charts at the Windscale nuclear plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Windscale was the old name of the Sellafield nuclear plant in Cumbria; here it is split as 'wind scale', the Beaufort scale, on which force 1 has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerful melody is a carefree song; force 1 on the Beaufort scale is the faintest breeze.

clue.text: Assembly-rooms Mum chooses, of no variety

indicators.note: of no variety is a playful signal: the letters of the preceding words are given a different arrangement

explanation.surface: The halls Mum picks are dull and all alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges the fourteen letters of MUM CHOOSES OF NO. 'Assembly' is the legislative kind: the lower chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower chamber of the British Parliament is an elected assembly, and also the building where it sits.

clue.text: All-male race? That will get us nowhere!

definitions.note: an exclamation standing for a state of no progress

parts.note: a stag party is for men only
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A people consisting only of men could never have descendants.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-male people would produce no children, so would go nowhere: the definition doubles as a comment on the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Standstill or lack of development leaves things going nowhere.

clue.text: Match trumps in card-game

definitions.meaning: a match is a marriage, as in a good match
in the game Pope Joan, the king and queen of trumps held together are given this name

explanation.surface: A partnership won by trumps in a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a marriage; in Pope Joan the trump king and queen together are named after wedlock.

clue.text: Defence fair people listen to?

definitions.meaning: a justification or excuse offered for an action
fair-minded people are said to listen to good sense and argument

explanation.surface: A defence that impartial people pay attention to.
explanation.definitionFit: A justification given for an act is a defence; sensible people heed rational argument.

clue.text: Severe form of gastric trouble

indicators.note: form of says the answer takes shape from letters inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bad case of stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and stern both describe rules or people allowing no leniency.

clue.text: Approach-lines of Don Juan, for example

parts.note: tone is the manner or approach taken, as in the tone of a letter
a poem is made of lines of verse

explanation.surface: The chat-up lines of the legendary seducer Don Juan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach-lines' suggests a seducer's patter, but Don Juan here is Richard Strauss's orchestral piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Strauss's Don Juan is a single-movement orchestral work telling a story, the symphonic form Liszt invented.

clue.text: Pictures indexed sometimes?

parts.note: read index as the index finger: images made by that finger's tip pressed in ink, as police record them

explanation.surface: Photographs that are occasionally catalogued in an index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indexed' suggests a catalogue; it means made by the index finger, as when police take prints.
explanation.definitionFit: Police take inked impressions of the fingertips, often the index finger, to identify people.

clue.text: Establishes business with sums of money in hand

definitions.meaning: to float a company is to launch it, often by issuing shares
a float is cash kept for giving change at the start of trading

explanation.surface: Sets up a firm with cash available.
explanation.definitionFit: Launching a company on the stock market is floating it; a till's starting change is its float.

clue.text: Mind this part of autopsy check?

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pathologist asks whether the brain should be examined during a post-mortem.
explanation.walkthrough: Mind this is the definition: the answer, mind, is literally part of the words autopsy check.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for soul is used for the human mind or spirit.

clue.text: Holy rest, perhaps, provided by The Tabard Inn

definitions.note: the Southwark inn where Chaucer's pilgrims gather, an example of the answer

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters of holy rest might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: The Tabard Inn offers pilgrims a holy rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HOLY REST. In The Canterbury Tales the pilgrims set out from the Tabard Inn in Southwark, London.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a hotel or tavern, and Chaucer's Tabard is a famous one.

clue.text: Shelter king with national emblem

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch takes refuge with his country's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The leek is the national emblem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales has the vegetable as its symbol, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Plant in neat border

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox is one
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A plant in a tidy flowerbed edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild primula, a flowering plant related to the cowslip.

clue.text: Recline with female? Gladly, in the old days!

parts.note: to lie is to recline

explanation.surface: Lying down with a woman was a pleasure in times gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb meant willingly, as in 'I would as lief stay'.

clue.text: Walked purposefully in Dorset resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so the letters of Dorset are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone striding along the front at a Dorset seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town, but it is 're-sort', rearranging DORSET; Dorset is an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To stride is to walk with long, decisive steps.

clue.text: Coward's allergic reaction

definitions.meaning: a work by Noël Coward, the English playwright: his 1925 comedy
an allergy to pollen causing sneezing

explanation.surface: A timid person's allergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person, but it is Noël Coward, whose comedy has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward wrote the comedy of that title; pollen allergy brings sneezing and streaming eyes.
